**Voica v0.9.1 — when the correction model is refused, one retry and no longer wait.**

### Fixed: a refusal no longer multiplies the wait

0.9.0 taught AI term correction to step down to the next model when Groq refuses one — a model not
enabled for your organisation (`403`) or withdrawn (`404`) — and to retry the same dictation there, so
its correction is not lost.

It stepped too eagerly: with several refusals in a row it kept trying model after model, each with its
own 20-second timeout, while you waited for the text.

Now it is **exactly one retry**, and both requests share **one** time budget. If the retry fails as
well, the text goes as it is — nothing is ever blocked by correction — and the next dictation starts
straight on a working model. It costs one extra request, once.

A model you **picked yourself** is still never swapped for another, not even for one dictation: you
get the notice, the text goes without correction, and your choice stays.

### Install

Windows 10 1809+ / x64:

| File | Size | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **`Voica-Setup-0.9.1.exe`** | ~75 MB | nothing — recommended |
| `Voica.exe` | ~80 MB | nothing — single file, no installation |
| `Voica-fx.exe` | ~37 MB | [.NET 8 Desktop Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) installed once |

Installing over an existing copy keeps your history, settings and API key.

Not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn → **More info → Run anyway**
([why, and how to verify](https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win#why-does-windows-warn-about-this-app)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
